note: Extraction from Robert Brandom's Making It Explicit applied to KnowledgeOS: models knowledge-bearing discourse via commitment/entitlement/inference/challenge/scorekeeping rather than fact-storage, proposes a Commitment Ledger derived structure and an Inferential Content Principle plus an Explicitness Principle; seventh/eighth book in the McGinn/Floridi/Dretske/Fagin/Gärdenfors/Searle/Williamson research arc (S0520 roadmap), explicitly complementary to (not competing with) the Williamson non-reduction result.

aliases: Gelfond & Kahl Knowledge Representation, Reasoning, and the Design of Intelligent Agents lens
note: Extraction from Gelfond & Kahl's knowledge representation/ASP textbook applied to KnowledgeOS: separates declarative representation from reasoning algorithms, grounds UNKNOWN/nonmonotonic reasoning/defaults/diagnosis/elaboration-tolerance/open-vs-closed-world computationally, derives K-INV-08..K-INV-15, and proposes an Epistemic Model Separation Principle plus a four-part Knowledge Space/History/Epistemic Model/Knowledge Claim architecture; described as a 'major refinement' rather than just another lens.

A specific formal-Kernel adjudication candidate (C-15, on how knowledge retraction should be modeled) reframed via the Knowledge Space + time-indexed Projection idea; discusses whether retraction is an epistemic-state transition, a lifecycle/process attribute orthogonal to epistemic status, or a projection-relative absence; explicitly held as a brainstorming hypothesis (C-15-H1) not yet an adjudicated ruling, pending falsification testing against v1.1, identity, history, authority, and the ZERO lens.

aliases: Knowledge Element / Knowledge Measurement Vector research model
note: S0565's mathematical research model defining a knowledge element as a tuple (proposition, participant, context, time, regime, evidence, derivation, status) and proposing a multidimensional Knowledge Measurement Vector (logical support, probabilistic support, unknownness, provenance, inferential centrality, conflict, stability, margin, coverage, explanatory gain) instead of one scalar 'knowledge score'; proposes distance/flux/depth/agreement metrics between knowledge states and a strict Kernel-stores-substrate/regimes-compute-metrics separation.

aliases: Brachman & Levesque Knowledge Representation and Reasoning lens
note: Extraction from Brachman & Levesque's Knowledge Representation and Reasoning applied to KnowledgeOS: grounds the infinite-belief/finite-representation distinction, representation != knowledge, knowledge-level vs symbol-level, explicit vs implicit knowledge (Explicitness Principle), and the Expressiveness-Tractability tradeoff; part of the S0520 seven-book research roadmap (fifth of Floridi/Williamson/Dretske/Fagin/Brachman-Levesque/Brandom/Searle).

Refines an earlier 'correct/incorrect' formulation into 'Knowledge enables a participant to discriminate among competing possibilities, select relevant/trustworthy information, and act/reason accordingly', proposing task-specific discrimination/selection/decision-accuracy measures D(K)/S(K)/A(K) and a Kernel-preserves-structures/regimes-perform-discrimination boundary.

Proposes treating the Knowledge Space as a measurable space (Ω,𝓕) and a participant's knowledge projection as a measure/distribution/field μ_{A,t,R,C} over it (coverage/evidence/confidence/relevance/uncertainty measures kept separate, never one universal Knowledge(B) number), with knowledge density k_A(x,t), a continuity-equation-style flow model, epistemic distance between participants' projections, coverage-gap and projection-coherence-under-refinement measures, and an explicit warning that measure theory supplies quantities but not the semantics of knowledge -- Epistemology/Semantics -> Measurable Structure -> Measurement, never the reverse.

Extraction from Fred S. Roberts' Measurement Theory applied to KnowledgeOS: measurement as a homomorphism from an empirical relational system to a numerical one (representation + uniqueness problems), nominal/ordinal/interval/ratio/absolute scale types with their admissible transformations, perfect-substitute equivalence and quotienting, extensive/conjoint/difference measurement conditions for when addition/aggregation/subtraction are meaningful, and a resulting Measurement Meaningfulness Invariant and Scale-Safety Principle; corrects the earlier Knowledge Measurement Vector work by showing Truth and epistemic distance are not automatically ratio/absolute-scaled.

aliases: Aggoun & Elliott Measure Theory and Filtering lens
note: Extraction from Aggoun & Elliott's Measure Theory and Filtering applied to KnowledgeOS v0.2: proposes identifying a knowledge projection with conditional expectation Π_{A,t}=E[K|ℱ^A_t], participant-relative knowledge with change-of-measure/Radon-Nikodym derivatives dP_A/dP_B, knowledge evolution with an Ito SDE and martingale decomposition, stopping times for admission/retraction/change events, and quadratic variation as a knowledge-noise measure; collapses the earlier four-spaces (Ω_S,Ω_E,Ω_D,Ω_A) proposal into one probability space with different filtrations. NOTE: a subsequent document (S0575) explicitly titled 'knowledge is not conditional expectation — correction' challenges this document's central identification; record as a source claim, not an established result.

A governed research extraction (non-authoritative) reconstructing 'What is Knowledge?' from the full 250-document brainstorming corpus (Phase 1 root 99 docs + Phase 2 kernel 151 docs), using three explicitly separated registers (⟦C⟧ corpus-says, ⟦I⟧ inferred, ⟦L⟧ formal-law-as-comparison-target-only); finds ~10 competing conceptions (K-1..K-11: stored-content/rejected, relationship, state-evolution, pipeline, Cognitive-Worlds, factive-relation-to-Knowledge-Space, capacity, continuous-flow, measure-over-space, institutional, primitive/unanalysable), identifies K-4/K-7/K-9 as incompatible with any identity-bearing Kernel aggregate, and K-11 (Williamson primitivism) as denying the corpus's whole definitional field; corrects its own earlier claim about when 'Knowledge Space' first appears (Phase 1 vocabulary precedent 20260822-0200 is a different concept, not absence).

The accumulating one-document-at-a-time research ledger for the Knowledge concept reconstruction (successor practice to KNOWLEDGE-CONCEPT-EXTRACTION-001, S0577): tracks a model-change log (K-M0 inherited starting model -> K-M1 after document 1, change type M2 EXTEND), a concept register (KCON-001..005) with provenance/status/challenger fields, a recorded-not-resolved contradiction (C-K1: knowledge as understanding vs knowledge as relationship), and six explicit non-mergeable registers (RESEARCH FACT / RESEARCH HYPOTHESIS / EXTERNAL THEORY / PROJECT CONCEPT / ARCHITECTURAL PRESSURE / FORMAL ARCHITECTURE).

Major architectural revision responding to a critique of the measure-theory-as-foundation line (S0568-S0576): defines the KnowledgeOS core as a many-sorted relational/temporal/logical structure (participants, contexts, time, domain objects, information, epistemic states, typed relations, history/transitions) with knows(a,p,c,t) as a primitive semantic relation constrained by factivity, and models mathematical regimes (logical/probabilistic/metric/topological/measure/institutional) as structure-adding 'functors' F_R over the core rather than as the core itself; integrates DDD bounded-context/anti-corruption discipline, a Zero-Lens admission test, and Roberts' measurement governance as a cross-cutting gate; gives a final five-layer architecture (Domain/Core Epistemic Structure/Representation-Projection/Mathematical Regime/Evaluation-Decision) and a new invariant 'no mathematical regime may silently redefine a core semantic concept.'

A governed finding-document series (docs/knowledgeos/reviews/kernel/session1/ and session2/) recording discrete, individually-adjudicable research findings from re-reading the brainstorming corpus, each with a Finding class (RESEARCH FACT / MEASURED CURRENT-STATE EVIDENCE), Status (OPEN), lens tags, source/provenance table, ⟦C⟧/⟦I⟧/⟦L⟧ registers, and explicit 'not adjudicated, not architecture' framing; distinct from the KNOWLEDGE-CONCEPT-EXTRACTION-001/Reconstruction-Ledger track (S0577/S0580) though using the same register discipline.

aliases: Kernel Brainstorming Corpus Phase A Census
note: The canonical Phase A classification census of the kernel/ brainstorming corpus (158 documents at latest count): a four-dimension per-document classification scheme (Subject/Altitude/Epistemic-role/Kernel-relevance), a verified duplicate register, twelve content clusters, a seven-item (later eight) recurring-temptation register T-1..T-8, and a K3/K4 candidate subset — referenced throughout the batch's classification-artifact family (dependency-map.md, cluster-map.md, contradiction-map.md, corpus-index.md).

Phase B classification artifact companion to the Phase A census: maps response-chains and chronology anomalies across the kernel corpus via content inference (since the corpus is almost entirely unlinked by explicit citation), records structural observations (two corpus regions, extraction near-independence, convergence points, S-4: falsification is rare/external) later itself falsified by the measure-theory-thread self-attack (T-8, S0586).

notations: SOURCE -> CLASSIFIED -> SYNTHESIZED -> ADVERSARIAL -> ARCHITECTURAL AUTHORITY
note: A recurring governance invariant stamped on every kernel-corpus directory README: a document never acquires a later status because of the directory it sits in; status advances only by a recorded act; directory names express artifact function, never subject or authority; source classification is metadata recorded in a census, never a path or filename code.
